claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
The initial alloy contains 30–40 at.% Fe, 30–40 at.% Co, and 30–40 at.% Ni.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi has a coercive field no greater than 100 Oe.
The intervention introduces coherent nanoprecipitates into the FCC FeCoNi matrix.
The introduced nanoprecipitates are 5–10 nm in size.
The introduced nanoprecipitates occupy a volume fraction of 0.05–0.10.
The introduced nanoprecipitates have Fe3O4 composition.
The nanoprecipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
Magnetic-domain-wall pinning and nucleation caused by the nanoprecipitates increase coercivity.
Introducing the specified Fe3O4 nanoprecipitates will increase coercive field by at least 50% relative to the baseline alloy.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will have a coercive field of at least 150 Oe.
Previous studies on similar systems support the proposed domain-wall-pinning and nucleation mechanism.
Magnetic measurements are to be performed at 20 ± 1 °C.
Magnetic measurements are to be performed in a zero-applied-field environment.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on nanoprecipitate properties and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The conditions require a zero-applied-field environment, whereas measuring a magnetic hysteresis loop and coercive field ordinarily requires sweeping an applied magnetic field. The intended measurement protocol is therefore internally inconsistent or inadequately specified.
